title: First real-solver results (real FNO + real spectral; stub M1/M2)
setup: real FNO surrogate + verified spectral corrector, SyntheticTrust + CouplingStub, test ICs 900-909

findings.extrapolation_error_cut: pure FNO ~14% (cost study) -> hybrid ~0.75-0.97% : long-horizon error cut ~15-18x
findings.knob_traces_tradeoff: tighter target raises cost (1.05->1.17) and lowers error (0.97%->0.75%)
findings.honest_hit_rate: 100% for targets >= 0.02; 80% at 0.01 (accuracy floor ~0.75%, so 0.01 is near the limit)
findings.error_floor: ~0.75% = FNO in-window error, uncorrected by the stub coupling (expected)

caveats: baseline points (pure-ML, pure-numerical) still to be added via partial_baselines()

honest_comparison.corrected_framing: With REAL solvers the hybrid is a genuine TRADE-OFF filling the middle of the frontier - NOT free numerical-grade accuracy (that was an artifact of the idealized stand-in). It cuts ML's 7.8% error to <1% at ~1/3 of numerical cost, but does not reach numerical's 0.01%.
